version: Published October 2015; reviewed May 2021; updated July 2024
notes: Accessible full text supports ABCDE as a structured assessment approach for deteriorating or critically ill patients, regular reassessment, early additional help, and team communication. UK professional guidance; used only to explain the general assessment framework. Specific interventions, targets, and procedures are not imported into this Philippine Nursing study material.

title: Infection and Neutropenia during Cancer Treatment
authority: National Cancer Institute, U.S. National Institutes of Health
version: Online page reviewed 23 January 2020; full text checked 22 October 2026
notes: Accessible NCI text is specifically about cancer and cancer treatment. It says cancer/treatments such as chemotherapy can increase infection risk, lists infection signs including fever and chills, advises contacting the health team, and notes infection during cancer treatment can be life-threatening. Page review date is 23 January 2020; currentness requires human verification. It does not support claims about every immunosuppressive drug, Philippine protocols, or a universal numeric threshold.

title: 5.11 Weight-Based Calculations — Nursing Skills 2e
authority: Open RN; Wisconsin Technical Colleges System
version: Nursing Skills 2e, §5.11; full text checked 22 October 2026
notes: Accessible full text supports weight-based dose arithmetic, dimensional analysis, converting units, calculating liquid volume from a labeled concentration, checking label/weight, and separate dose verification. U.S. open textbook; it does not establish Philippine medication authority, a specific medication dose/range, or local policy.

title: 6.1 Introduction to Safe Range / Weight-Based — Nursing Dosage Calculations
authority: WisTech Open; Wisconsin Technical Colleges System
version: Nursing Dosage Calculations, §6.1; full text checked 22 October 2026
notes: Accessible full text distinguishes mg/kg/dose from mg/kg/day and explains that validating an order requires medication-specific range, frequency, maximum daily amount, route, formulation, and other guidance. The textbook’s clinical examples and ranges are not imported into BoardPrep; use is limited to the arithmetic-versus-order-validity distinction.

title: Frequently Asked Questions About Suicide
authority: National Institute of Mental Health, U.S. National Institutes of Health
version: NIH Publication No. 23-MH-6389; revised 2023; full text checked 22 October 2026
notes: Full text supports taking suicide talk and warning signs seriously, asking directly about suicidal thoughts, recognizing plans/means and giving away possessions as warning signs, staying with a person who says they intend suicide, not promising secrecy, collaborative safety planning/follow-up, and safe storage of lethal means. U.S. public guidance; U.S. emergency numbers and service pathways are excluded and no Philippine legal or clinical protocol is inferred.
